title: Pew finds more Americans see China ahead of the US in AI
friendlyTitle: Many Americans think China leads in AI, but one-third are unsure
summary: In a June survey of 3,488 US adults, 36% said China was more advanced in AI, 12% chose the United States, 18% saw them as equal and 33% were unsure. Separately, 43% said US leadership in AI was extremely or very important, while 51% expected AI to widen the gap between rich and poor countries.
friendlySummary: A Pew survey found that 36% of US adults think China is ahead in AI and 12% think the US is ahead. One-third were not sure, and half expected AI to increase inequality between countries.
whyItMatters: Public expectations can shape investment, procurement and policy even when many people remain uncertain about the underlying technology. Businesses should prepare for stronger national-competition framing alongside concern that access to AI’s benefits will be uneven.
friendlyWhyItMatters: People’s beliefs about the AI race can affect government and business decisions. The results also show concern that richer countries may receive more of AI’s benefits.
